chitchat: The culvert wretch feeds a splinter to her small fire and watches it go.
"I went west once. I came back less. Ask me nothing else."
description: A wretch who lives deep in the culvert's mouth, wrapped in everything she owns, guarding a small fire and a smaller hope. She has been west, once, and it is the only thing she will talk about and the last thing she wants to.

bye.text: She turns back to her fire, done with you and with everything.

root.text: The wretch pulls her coats tighter and eyes you from beside her fire. "You're headed west, I can see it on you, you've got the look — the not-yet-scared look. I had it too. Warm yourself if you want. Then turn around."

west.text: Her eyes go somewhere else for a moment. "The neck. The killing floor above it. The things the neck lets down. I went up it on a dare and a full stomach and came back on my hands. Left something up there I'm not getting back. Don't make it two of us."

clothing_layers: a bundle of stolen coats worn all at once
rags bound at the wrist and ankle against the wind
a blanket that is more hole than blanket

name: a culvert wretch
